newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA warns Basque businesses to heed strike call.
newsitem.headline: ETA warns Basque businesses to heed strike call.

text.p: Basque separatist group ETA has warned Basque businessmen in Spain to heed a strike called for Friday which the regional government has outlawed, officials said.

Herri Batasuna (HB), the political arm of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), called the strike to protest at the imprisonment of its leadership. The Basque regional government warned on Tuesday that HB could intensify threats in coming days.
"The eventual success of the strike depends solely on HB's capacity to intimidate," Basque government spokeswoman Mari Carmen Garmendia told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting.

Basque businessmen have long complained they receive threats from ETA to pay a "revolutionary tax". Businessmen in the region have frequently been targets of kidnappings and attacks in the rebels' 29-year campaign for an independent state.
Business owners said on Tuesday they had received letters from HB explaining the need for solidarity and warning there would be consequences for those who do not heed the strike.
A business association in Guipuzcoa province denounced the threats and called on members to ignore the strike call.

HB's entire 25-person leadership was summoned last month by the Supreme Court on charges of distributing an illegal pro-ETA video during Spain's 1996 election campaign. They ignored the summons and 18 were jailed for failing to appear in court.

Residents in the northern Basque country said tension was mounting and walls were filled with strike graffiti and placards. The labour union linked to ETA staged a protest march through the town of San Sebastian during the day.
The regional government declared the strike illegal, saying its motive was solely political. It urged citizens to overcome the fear of threats and go to work as usual.
"The aim, as those who called it have already said, is to provoke agitation and upheaval in the Basque society," said Garmendia.
Officials said the government would use the police and all other legal means to ensure businesses, public transport and traffic functioned normally.
